$comment: The vendor feed list. Adding a fifth Statuspage vendor is a line here and no code —
server/src/adapters/vendorstatus/index.test.ts proves it by loading a five-entry list.
'platform' selects the adapter and is never inferred from 'id'.
'url' must be https: this process fetches exactly what this file says and nothing else.
'component' is optional; when present the feed MUST publish it, or the vendor reads
unknown rather than quietly rolling up a shorter list.
Statuspage: use /api/v2/summary.json, never /api/v2/status.json — the latter is a
page-level rollup with no components, incidents or maintenance.
Zendesk: the url is the SSP base; the adapter appends /incidents.json and, only when a
Milestone 3. index.ts answers for them with an explicit unsupported-platform error, so
adding them here before the adapter exists reads unknown rather than green.

Zendesk: 'tenants' scopes the feed per account via ?subdomain=. We have two — crexendo and netsapiens — and BOTH are queried and merged, deduped by incident id. They share Pod 23 today, so one query would happen to cover both; that coincidence is exactly what not to build on.

proofpoint is Hornetsecurity on status.io (live.hornet-status.com); the page id is in its HTML. 'locations' filters to OUR datacentres — the feed publishes ten and an unfiltered Frankfurt outage would land on our tile. Ours is named two mutually-exclusive ways: 'United States - Atlanta' carries the 13 core email services, 'United States - Georgia' the 3 newer 365 products. Both, or a third of the estate drops out.

m365 is Graph service health, app-only auth by certificate — the only feed needing a credential, which lives outside the repo (see http/graphToken.ts). 'components' names the 7 services we depend on out of the 32 Graph reports: Microsoft always has something degraded somewhere (9 of 32 on 2026-09-19, three of them Copilot), and rolling up all of them would leave the tile permanently amber.
